papers.title: Infrared thermal imaging to determine temperature parameters of dengue vector habitats across ecological regions of Nepal: a pilot feasibility study
papers.summary: Dengue is a major vector-borne disease in Nepal, driven by container-breeding Aedes mosquitoes that thrive in domestic, urban settings.  Its risk is increasing from the lowland Terai to the Hill and Mountain regions due to urbanisation and global warming.
papers.mainFinding: Thermal imaging shows promise for the field characterisation of mosquito breeding sites, but it is not interchangeable with standard thermometry without qualification, including calibration and uncertainty analysis.
papers.whyItMatters: Conceptual or methodological relevance to mosquito eco-evolution and vector ecology.

papers.title: Temperature variation as a driver of Wolbachia release efficacy: implications for dengue control in warming climates
papers.summary: Background Wolbachia-based control methods reduce dengue transmission by suppressing Aedes aegypti populations or blocking viral replication, yet their effectiveness across the climatic conditions of endemic regions remains poorly understood.  Seasonal and interannual temperature changes shape mosquito dynamics, but how Wolbachia releases perform during anomalous events such as El Nino or heatwaves is largely unknown a gap that limits our ability to optimize release strategies and predict intervention success across different climates.
papers.mainFinding: By elucidating the mechanistic interplay among temperature, Wolbachia, and dengue, our findings help refine Wolbachia release programs to suit different climatic conditions, thereby strengthening dengue control as climate variability intensifies.
papers.whyItMatters: Conceptual or methodological relevance to mosquito eco-evolution and vector ecology.
papers.readFirstReason: Ranked highly for context-dependent mosquito biocontrol, temperature-dependent control efficacy.

papers.title: Distinct Swimming Behaviours in Pupae of Aedes, Anopheles and Culex Mosquitoes
papers.summary: The study quantified surface-swimming behaviour in pupae from 11 mosquito species. Aedes pupae generally moved slowly but frequently and explored more, whereas Anopheles and especially Culex pupae moved less often but swam faster and farther during each movement bout.
papers.mainFinding: Mosquito pupae are not an ecologically passive stage; their movement strategies differ consistently among genera and may reflect adaptation to different aquatic habitats.
papers.whyItMatters: Pupal mobility can change exposure to predators, sampling devices, habitat edges, and emergence conditions. It is a strong conceptual and methodological paper for interpreting predator encounters and control efficiency in urban-rural mesocosms.
papers.readFirstReason: Ranked highly for aquatic behaviour affecting predator exposure.

papers.title: Insight into eco-epidemiological traits of European native vector mosquitoes for disease transmission
papers.taxon: Culex pipiens and other native European mosquitoes
papers.summary: This open-access primer synthesizes the distribution, larval habitats, host-seeking and host preferences, overwintering strategies, hybridization, and vector competence of native European mosquitoes. It places native Culex mosquitoes at the centre of Europe’s expanding West Nile virus risk and identifies major ecological and surveillance gaps.
papers.mainFinding: European transmission risk is increasingly shaped by native mosquito vectors, while incomplete information on their ecological ranges and life-history traits still limits surveillance and risk assessment.
papers.whyItMatters: This is the strongest framing paper for connecting Belgian Culex pipiens ecology, urban habitat use, host interactions, climate sensitivity, and population structure to WNV emergence and spatial expansion in Europe.
papers.readFirstReason: Ranked highly for European vector-trait synthesis, European WNV/SINV dynamics, European Culex population structure.
papers.vectorSpecies: Native European mosquitoes, especially Culex spp. including Culex pipiens
papers.hostSpecies: Avian reservoir hosts; humans and horses as incidental hosts
papers.studyPeriod: Primer and evidence synthesis; WNV distribution examples include data through 3 December 2025
papers.europeanTransmissionRisk: Shows how well-adapted native Culex vectors support sustained WNV transmission and expansion into newly affected European regions.

papers.title: Comprehensive Evaluation of Bacillus thuringiensis subsp. israelensis: From Molecular Profiling to Ecotope-Specific Larvicidal Efficacy Against Laboratory Aedes aegypti and Wild Mosquito Populations
papers.taxon: Aedes aegypti and wild mosquito populations
papers.summary: Three native Bacillus thuringiensis subsp. israelensis H14 strains were molecularly profiled and tested against laboratory Aedes aegypti and wild mosquito larvae. Controlled exposure produced approximately 95–96% mortality within 48 hours, followed by comparisons across forest and steppe mosquito populations.
papers.mainFinding: The Bti strains combined stable Cry and Cyt toxin production with strong larvicidal activity, although efficacy varied with strain and ecological setting.
papers.whyItMatters: The study offers endpoints and assay structure for testing context-dependent mosquito control, but laboratory and regional field efficacy should not be treated as proof of persistence or non-target safety in Belgian urban ponds.
